samples.identification: Bitmap-concealed multistage CLR loader carrying an unrelated Microsoft signature
execution_trace: Entry MethodDef 7 (wait_Down, RVA 0x2093) starts a WinForms form. Its initialization sets Opacity=0 and ShowIcon=false; Load reaches MethodDef 8 at RVA 0x239c.

capital_Paul selects manifest resources and ResourceReader entries by comparing the first 16 bytes of their ASCII SHA-1 digests. Bitmap resource data is traversed bottom-up by rows, with B,G,R bytes appended and a four-byte little-endian payload length.
MethodDef 9 at RVA 0x24c8 XORs every byte with key[i % key.Length]. Applying its caller's key to the first PNG (42x42, file offset 0xa61) recovers a 5120-byte managed PE, assembly tmp619B.
The outer stub loads that PE through AppDomain.Load, takes its first exported type, then sets the checkbox Checked property. CheckedChanged executes MethodDef 6 at RVA 0x21dc.

That handler instantiates the exported type with a second bitmap and a key/IV. The helper reconstructs the second bitmap (513x513, file offset 0x1ab9), applies RijndaelManaged.CreateDecryptor/TransformFinalBlock, and removes a nine-byte QuickLZ stored-mode envelope (not a compressed-data branch).

The resulting 787456-byte managed PE has SHA256 36ec632b5e6831bac2ef6b7a93768cb016844933a1b97bba51644565fb860410. The outer handler retrieves its byte-array field, loads it into the AppDomain, creates a ThreadStart delegate from Assembly.EntryPoint and calls Thread.Start.

The retained Microsoft PKCS#7 signer is unrelated to the new program identity. Signature metadata verifies the signed structure, while the computed image digest mismatches the signed digest. Hidden multistage code activation plus transplanted signing, rather than entropy or a family label, establishes the verdict.
limits: Final-stage identifiers are ConfuserEx-style Unicode obfuscation. No credential-theft, ransomware, C2 endpoint or malware-family claim is inferred for this stage.
Delivery provenance, authorization, endpoint reachability and runtime success are unknown.
final_hostile_behaviors: Bitmap resource to managed assembly entry-point activation
Microsoft signing-trust masquerade over a mismatched image digest

samples.identification: CosmicDuke/BotGenStudio concealed native credential stealer with Chrome version-resource disguise
execution_trace: CRT entry 0x4089eb reaches loader 0x401170. The loader reads its size-prefixed buffer at VA 0x42b3d0 (file offset 0x2a7d0), reconstructs the native stage and restores saved registers/stack before an indirect tail handoff.

Independent bounded raw-Snappy decoding consumes 126032 bytes and produces 179432 bytes. The native PE starts at decoded offset 0x2e8; its SHA256 is 9e3c407d3bbf2a69cf6509994ffb17b45c58c3adaf3dc876b23e7d0575e24ca0.

Recovered PE 0x4110ef discovers Firefox installation paths. 0x410f11 resolves NSS_Init, PK11SDR_Decrypt, NSSBase64_DecodeBuffer and SQLite calls into a dispatch table through native library/export resolution.

0x4114d2 opens signons.sqlite and submits SELECT id, hostname, usernamefield, passwordfield, encryptedusername, encryptedpassword FROM moz_logins to the SQLite callback at 0x411258. The callback uses 0x41119f to Base64-decode and NSS-decrypt the selected credentials, then packages the host/user/password records.

The recovered PE registers raw input at 0x407cc0, retrieves raw input in its message handlers and translates keyboard state through ToUnicodeEx at 0x407b3a. This is actual native code, rather than an attribution from packed string fragments.

The outer file claims Chrome/Google while running concealed credential acquisition code. BotGenStudio build-path and distinctive cipher-key evidence corroborate family identity; the supplied filename and sandbox score are not used as proof.
limits: The supplied UPX sections are populated and have a reconstructed .imports section. Their low entropy does not prove a fake packer or fabricated provenance.
The scan also extracts an embedded Windows CALC.EXE component; it has no hostile findings and does not determine the outer verdict.

Installation context and authorization are absent. Credential recovery alone has legitimate uses, but the concealment, credential-record collection and false browser identity tip this specimen toward malware.
changes: Retire unsubstantiated-vendor-claim-fake-packer: generic vendor text plus low-entropy UPX labels establishes neither a false vendor claim nor packer deception. Keep every vendor/layout atom and the independently supported credential-theft, Chrome-disguise and family findings.

samples.identification: Disclosed example-domain composite GitHub Action for shell-stage fetching
execution_trace: The complete archive has action.yml (335 bytes) and setup.sh (55 bytes); neither contains obfuscation or an additional payload.

The description explicitly says Fetches and runs the stage. The first sequential bash step downloads https://example.com/stage.sh to stage.sh and invokes bash stage.sh; the second pipes the same URL's response to sh. setup.sh contains the same pipeline.

These are real network and execution capabilities. No bytes establish stealing, spying, backdoors, destruction, deceptive packaging, or concealment. CI context and an unrecognized installer URL do not supply those missing claims.
limits: Remote response contents and real deployment provenance are not supplied. The verdict is about this disclosed illustrative artifact, not a guarantee for arbitrary future downloaded scripts.
The collector's controls filename is not used as verdict evidence; changing the endpoint spelling does not restore hostile intent.
